learning_outcomes.text: Integrate knowledge and face the complexity of forming judgments from information that, being incomplete or limited, includes reflections on the social and ethical responsibilities linked to the application of their knowledge and judgments.
Communicate their conclusions and the knowledge and ultimate reasons that support them to specialized and non-specialized audiences clearly and unambiguously.
Possess the learning skills that allow them to continue studying in a way that will largely be self-directed or autonomous.
Ability to apply acquired knowledge and solve problems in new or little-known environments within broader and multidisciplinary contexts, being able to integrate knowledge.
Ability to communicate (orally and in writing) conclusions and the knowledge and ultimate reasons that support them to specialized and non-specialized audiences clearly and unambiguously.
Possess skills for continuous, self-directed and autonomous learning.
Ability to understand and know how to apply the functioning and organization of the Internet, new generation Internet technologies and protocols, component models, middleware, and services.
Know and use the fundamentals of programming in telecommunication networks and services.
Select the most appropriate transport layer protocol for a given application.
Know the most important architectures used in the implementation of distributed applications and select the most appropriate for a given application.
Design and program component-based and service-oriented distributed applications.
Know different integration patterns and their solutions.
Select the most appropriate middleware to solve specific integration problems.
Effectively communicate (in expression and comprehension), orally and in writing, the characteristics of the designed distributed services.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to distributed systems. Development technologies.
Architecture of distributed applications. Communication models.
Programming practices for communications in a distributed system.
Practices on classic distributed architectures (client-server, peer to peer, event-oriented programming).
Practices on data standards and adapters (XML, JSON, scraping).
Practices on middleware and integration standards (RESTful).
Practices on microservices deployment (APIs, containers, Cloud).
assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, the theory grade (TEO) is (T1+T2)/2, and the practical grade (PRAC) is (PRAC1+PRAC2)/2. A minimum grade of 5.0 out of 10 is required for TEO, PRAC, and TG. If all minimums are met, the final grade is calculated as 0.4 * TEO + 0.3 * PRAC + 0.3 * TG; otherwise, the grade is the minimum of the calculated score and 4.0. For the extraordinary call, there is a single on-site exam (PP) that covers both theoretical and practical content, and a minimum grade of 5.0 out of 10 is required for PP. The final grade is calculated as 0.7 * PP + 0.3 * TG; otherwise, the grade is the minimum of the calculated score and 4.0. Students with differentiated evaluation are exempt from group work, and their ordinary final grade is 0.50 * TEO + 0.50 * PRAC, while their extraordinary final grade is 100% PP.
